params.body:
The worksheet conversation now carries every current site (199) and the screen offers no shortcuts. The costing replay in #51 showed what the past predicts:

- a worker's four most recent sites hold tonight's site 73% of the time;
- the ten machines he and that site used most hold 89% of the machines booked;
- articles per site are weak (twenty cover half), so articles are not suggested.

This PR builds on those numbers.

**Reference data from Bouwsoft** (`reference:sync`, daily at 05:30, after `sites:sync`)
- `ReferenceSource` gains `people()`, `machines()`, `articles()` and `bookings(since)`. `ReferenceSync` applies the same rules as `SiteSync`:
  - it matches on the external id, or the first time on the code;
  - it switches rows off and never deletes them;
  - it never touches the paper tally sheet (`on_sheet`);
  - an empty answer fails that part only.
- Staff list: only id, number, name and active are requested (`columns`), and only those are stored (`reference_people`).
- Catalogue:
  - the 402 Bouwsoft machines and the products are matched onto the August export rows by code;
  - a new machine whose name starts with "Huur" is marked as hired, which is how all 105 hired machines in the export are named.
- Costing: who, where, what and when for the last 70 days (`reference_bookings`). There are no quantities, prices or hours. Product lines carry no employee, because GLK records one value for all of them. Dates in the future are dropped.
- Read tools: `reference` (counts and last sync per part) and `reference_preview` (dry run). `health` now includes `referenceSync`.
- Office page **Ploeg** (`/ploeg`):
  - link a worker to a person on the staff list (one person is one worker);
  - add somebody from the staff list with a role and a language; the access code is generated.

**The flow**
- `Suggestions` ranks sites and machines by the number of days booked, with the most recent day breaking a tie. It combines two histories:
  - the costing, read over 21 days because it is entered about a week late;
  - his own worksheets in the app, read over 14 days.
- His fixed machine always comes first.
- On the worker screen:
  - "Op een van deze werven?" shows up to four site tiles, on the blank screen and on the board until a line has a site;
  - "Machines gebruikt? Tik ze aan" shows up to ten machine tiles.
  - A tap writes the row and dispatches `gekozen`. The running conversation then gets a system line naming the code or the exact name, and asks the next thing (`tell()` in both the OpenAI and ElevenLabs clients).
- `chosen_at` on worksheet lines and machine usages: a tapped row survives a reading made before the model heard about the tap. It is not frozen like a correction, because the hours he says next belong on it. Once a reading hands the row back, the flag clears and the row follows the model's picture again.
- The writer resolves a machine name that already stands on the sheet to that machine before the pair and rental gates. The model was told that exact name, so this is not a guess.
- The prompt lists his recent sites as recognition help only, and keeps the rule that it knows only today. The model never picks from the machine tiles itself.
- The speech hint leads with his own sites' names, clients, municipalities and streets, within the same 700 characters.

**After deploy:** run `php artisan reference:sync` once (or wait for 05:30), then link the workers on /ploeg.

Tests: 193/193. Checked on a phone-width screenshot locally: blank screen with site tiles, a tapped site, a tapped machine.
params.title: His recent sites and machines as tiles, from Bouwsoft's staff list, catalogue and costing
